comments.undefined:
The Atrial Fibrillation Monitoring Ontology (AFMO) extends the Personal Health Monitoring Ontology (PHMO) with concepts specific to atrial fibrillation (AF) monitoring.

From version 3.0, general personal health monitoring concepts have moved to the PHMO (http://purl.org/phmo), which the AFMO imports. Terms listed as deleted in the changelog have moved to the PHMO namespace.

In addition to the ontologies reused through the PHMO, the AFMO contains concepts reused from the following ontologies:

- Human Disease Ontology (DO)
- Medical Action Ontology (MAxO)

Health domain concepts have been manually cross-referenced to concepts from the Unified Medical Language System (UMLS) metathesaurus, which maps to several medical vocabularies and terminologies, including:

- SNOMED CT (US)
- Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) Thesaurus
- National Cancer Institute (NCI) Thesaurus
- MedlinePlus

- Smoker (a.k.a current smoker): a person who has smoked more than 100 cigarettes (including hand rolled cigarettes, cigars, cigarillos etc) in their lifetime and has smoked in the last 28 days. Includes daily and non-daily/social smokers.
- Non-smoker: composed of two groups: former smoker and never smoker.
   - Former smoker: a person who has smoked more than 100 cigarettes in their lifetime but has not smoked in the last 28 days. The international convention is to treat someone as an ex-smoker once they have been smokefree for one month (at least 28 days).
   - Never smoker: a person who has not smoked more than 100 cigarettes in their lifetime and does not currently smoke.

Dagfinn et al. (2018) noted that there is reduced risk of AF among former smokers compared to current smokers, but further research is needed to determine if the risk at some point reaches that of never smokers.

definition.value:
set of Observations or ObservationCollections; collections may be nested

  All Observation properties may appear in an Observation Collection, including: 
  hasFeatureOfInterest , hasUltimateFeatureOfInterest , usedProcedure , madeBySensor , observedProperty , phenomenonTime , startTime, resultTime , hasResult , hasSimpleResult : 
  If they are present, the value of these properties summarize the values of the matching properties of the member observations, where membership is either direct or transitive through one or more member observation collections. 
  The following consistency rules apply with respect to the Observation properties listed above: 
  
  1. Where an individual Observation Collection omits a property, a member Observation (direct or transitive) MAY have any value for that property.

  2. Where an individual Observation Collection has a single value for a property, each member Observation(direct or transitive) MUST have that same value for the property - i.e., the collection is homogeneous in that property.  That property MAY then be omitted in any member Observation or Observation Collection.

  3. Where an individual Observation Collection has more than one value for a property, each member Observation (direct or transitive) MUST have a value for that property that matches one of the values for the property in the collection. 
  
  4. Where an individual Observation Collection has a value for a property that is a range or interval, each member Observation (direct or transitive) MUST have a value for that property that matches or falls within that range or interval.

  5. Where an individual Observation Collection has more than one value for a property that is a range or interval, each member Observation (direct or transitive) MUST have a value for that property that either matches or falls within one of those ranges or intervals.
